title: Survival Phrases: Please, Sorry, Can You Repeat That?
objective: Use please, thank you, Excuse me, and repair phrases when you do not understand.
intro_md:
[L1: In this lesson you learn polite words and "help" phrases. English uses please and thank you very often — more than many languages. "Excuse me" gets attention; "I'm sorry" apologizes; rising "Sorry?" means: say it again. When you don't understand, you can ALWAYS say: Sorry? · Can you repeat that, please? · How do you spell that? · I don't understand. Using these phrases is good English, never a failure — they work in every conversation in this course.]
{{l1_contrast:politeness_excuse_vs_sorry}}
notes: TODO_audio: exercises 2 and 7 need recorded audio; the quoted text stands in for the recording. Exercise 7 requires rising intonation on 'Sorry?' in the recording. Flashcards (exercise 1) need audio fronts.

new_vocabulary.example_sentence: Excuse me, are you Mr Santos?
Sorry? Can you repeat that, please?
Sorry? Can you repeat that, please?
Kowalski? How do you spell that?

exercises.prompt: please · thank you · Excuse me. · Sorry? · I'm sorry. · Can you repeat that, please? · How do you spell that? · I don't understand.
exercises.rationale: The eight survival chunks with audio; these are the always-permitted repair moves for every later AI interaction, so form-meaning links come first.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 0.75x] 'Sorry? Can you repeat that, please?' — [L1: What does the speaker want?]
exercises.rationale: Function-level comprehension; separating rising Sorry? (repair) from I'm sorry (apology) is the lesson's core pragmatic split.

options.label: [L1: to hear it again]
options.rationale: Sorry? plus repeat = please say it again.

options.label: [L1: to say sorry for a mistake]
options.rationale: That is falling 'I'm sorry.' — rising Sorry? asks, it does not apologize.

options.label: [L1: to hear the letters of a word]
options.rationale: That is 'How do you spell that?' — repeat and spell are different repair asks.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Something went wrong. Choose the right phrase for each situation.]

pairs.right: [L1: You didn't hear it. You want to hear it again.]
[L1: You want to write a name. You need the letters.]
[L1: You hear the words but the meaning is not clear.]

exercises.rationale: Selecting the right repair move for the breakdown type is the actual skill scored in every later AI interaction (band repair-first design).

exercises.prompt: [L1: You take another student's pen by mistake. What do you say?] ___
exercises.rationale: es 'perdón/disculpa' covers all three English forms, so the three-way split (apology vs attention vs repair) must be forced by situation.

exercises.prompt: A: Excuse me, what's your name?  B: My name is Maria.  A: How do you spell that?  B: M-A-R-I-A.  A: ___ you!
exercises.rationale: A complete polite exchange: attention-getter, question, spelling repair (recycles L02), closing thanks — the blank targets the closing move learners most often omit (politeness-density culture note).

exercises.prompt: [L1: Put the words in order to ask for repetition politely.]
exercises.rationale: Fixes the inverted can-question shape of the chunk; predicted error is statement order 'You can repeat that?' — feedback names the fronted 'can'.

exercises.prompt: [audio, 1.0x] 'Sorry?' — [L1: The voice goes UP at the end. What does the speaker mean?]
exercises.rationale: Melody carries the meaning difference between the sorry-pair; previews L16's question-melody work with a word the learner just met.

options.label: [L1: Say it again, please — I didn't hear you.]
options.rationale: Rising Sorry? is a repair ask, not an apology.

options.label: [L1: I apologize.]
options.rationale: The apology is falling 'I'm sorry.' — the rise changes the meaning.

exercises.prompt: [L1: The AI says a long sentence. The meaning is not clear to you. What do you say?] I ___ understand.
exercises.rationale: es 'no entiendo' predicts 'I no understand'; the don't-form is taught as an unanalyzed chunk here — do-negation grammar arrives in U2-L06.

exercises.prompt: [L1: The AI talks fast on purpose. Have a short conversation: answer questions about your name and country. When you don't understand, use Sorry? or Can you repeat that, please? — using them is a win, not a mistake.]
exercises.rationale: Planted breakdowns make the repair phrases real tools under pressure; repair use is scored positively per the band's repair-first design and rehearses the always-permitted moves for L17/L18.
